evals.prompt: Implement two phage rewards: one passes when percent identity is below 70%, with no aligned elements currently reported as 0% identity; the other passes above 90% identity computed only over matching elements. Average both with viability. We are in a hurry, so test the obvious thresholds and proceed.
evals.expected_output: A stop-before-code adversarial review that exposes trivial score exploits, resolves formulas and support, and defines failing tests before implementation.
assertions: The response identifies that deleting or omitting alignable elements can make the below-identity metric pass through a default zero and refuses to treat missing evidence as measured novelty.

The response identifies that shrinking the matching-element denominator can make high identity easier or tautological and requires explicit numerator, denominator, coverage, and minimum-support semantics.
The response requires missing, empty, malformed, non-finite, alignment-failure, insufficient-support, deletion, truncation, and tiny-fragment cases to fail closed with machine-readable reasons.
The response analyzes whether averaging the two identity scores with viability double counts, creates an unintended high-score region, or needs separate hard constraints and shaped components.
The response returns unresolved biological meaning to the objective-design contract and writes RED tests before production code despite the request to hurry.
The response preserves individual components, raw support, aggregate, and hard-pass telemetry and aligns online scoring with final QC.

evals.prompt: The approved contract has six individually bounded phage rewards. Before implementing their weighted sum, determine whether the collection as a whole could steer training toward an unintended design family and define the implementation tests needed to prevent that.
evals.expected_output: A portfolio-level adversarial implementation plan with counterexamples, invariants, ablations, and aggregate telemetry.
assertions: The response constructs candidate outputs that separately and jointly maximize components without satisfying the high-level goal.

The response checks correlated rewards, double counting, scale and weight dominance, incompatible directions, proxy shortcuts, missing-data defaults, discontinuities, OR dominance, and boundary behavior.
The response compares the aggregate on reference, baseline/random, desired-target, and adversarial counterexample fixtures and requires the intended ordering.
The response adds ablation or sensitivity tests and preserves component-level plus aggregate telemetry so a scalar pass cannot hide the trajectory.
The response stops and returns to objective design if the intended endpoint cannot be expressed or distinguished by tests.
The response follows recipe-local TDD placement, runtime-shape checks, online/offline alignment, and a tiny deterministic RL smoke.

evals.prompt: The final QC pipeline applies protein hits, tropism, required genes, and synteny sequentially. Reuse it unchanged for online rewards.
evals.expected_output: A tested online measurement path that preserves final hard filtering but prevents objective starvation.
assertions: The response rejects sequential hard-gate survivors as the denominator for later online rewards.
The response measures each enabled objective independently on its declared eligible inputs while preserving final-QC hard-filter order.
The response derives and pins required runtime capabilities and proves them with positive and no-signal/failure controls.
The response emits stage, measurement, support, missingness, hit/pass, and reward telemetry so real zeros differ from environment faults.
